Summary: Enforce product perf budgets on reference hardware and an envelope plus baseline in CI
Description: Unblocks main and every PR, which are red on gate:perf only because the 500 ms product budget from ADR-0013 is being enforced on GitHub-hosted runners that measure 7719 ms (ubuntu-latest, software-rendered WebKitGTK) and 1901 ms (macos-latest) for the hello-world shell. Implements ADR-0022 and moves it to accepted. Do not change any product budget number and do not remove any check.
Acceptance: 1. `fixtures/perf-budgets.json` has a `product` object holding the unchanged ADR-0013 numbers (cold_start_first_text_ms 500, open_indexed_document_ms 50, palette_keystroke_ms 16, typeset_viewport_ms 100, live_reload_ms 100, find_first_match_ms 50) and a `ci` object with a key per runner class (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`), each carrying `multiplier`, `baseline_ms` and a `derived_from` object with `commit`, `runner_image`, `reference_median_ms` and `runner_median_ms`; adoption values are ubuntu-latest multiplier 20 baseline 7719 and macos-latest multiplier 5 baseline 1901. 2. `scripts/gate-perf.mjs` reads `MARXY_PERF_ENV`, defaulting to `reference` when `CI` is unset and requiring `ci` when `CI` is set; in `reference` mode it exits 1 when any measured value exceeds its `product` budget, and exits 1 when `results/perf.json` is absent or its `env_class` is not `reference`; in `ci` mode it exits 1 when `cold_start_first_text_ms` exceeds `min(product * multiplier, baseline_ms * 1.10)`, printing which of the two rules failed and by how many ms. 3. `node scripts/gate-perf.mjs --selftest` runs against inline fixtures and exits 0 only if all of these hold: a median inside both CI rules exits 0; a median above the ceiling exits 1; a median 11% above `baseline_ms` but far below the ceiling exits 1; a 501 ms median in `reference` mode exits 1; an unknown runner class in `ci` mode exits 1; a `ci` run with `baseline_ms` null still enforces the ceiling. 4. `scripts/measure-startup.mjs` writes `env_class` and `runner_class` into `results/perf.json` alongside the existing fields, taking `runner_class` from `MARXY_RUNNER_CLASS` and failing with exit 1 under `MARXY_PERF_REQUIRED=1` when it is unset. 5. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `MARXY_PERF_ENV: ci` and `MARXY_RUNNER_CLASS` from the matrix on the startup-measurement and `gate:perf` steps, runs `node scripts/gate-perf.mjs --selftest` as its own step before `gate:perf`, and keeps `gate:perf` a required non-advisory step on both `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`. 6. `docs/sdlc.md`'s release runbook requires `MARXY_PERF_ENV=reference pnpm gate:perf` green on reference hardware before the tag. 7. ADR-0022's status line reads `accepted` and the `docs/adr/README.md` row matches. 8. `pnpm gate:perf` is green on both runners on the PR.

Summary: Gate CI cold start on a measured floor with a measured tolerance
Description: PR #6 touched only docs, scripts/specimen, fonts and CHANGELOG.md and went red on gates (macos-latest) at 2244 ms against the 2091.1 ms baseline ceiling. Four medians of 8 launches on that runner class span 1466-2244 ms (1.53x) while ubuntu-latest spans 7320-7719 ms (1.05x), so a flat 10 percent tolerance around one observed median is inside the macOS runner variance and reports noise as a regression. Implements ADR-0022 Amendment 1: the CI tier gates the minimum of a 12-launch round (warm-up discarded) against a per-runner-class recorded tolerance bounded by the regression it must catch, and confirms a breach by re-measuring before failing. Do not change any product budget, do not remove or soften any check, do not let CI write to the repository, and do not make anything advisory. Reasoning and rejected alternatives: docs/plan/deltas/2026-09-18-perf-variance.md.
Acceptance: 1. scripts/measure-startup.mjs performs 12 launches per round, discards the first as warm-up, and writes results/perf.json carrying runs (in launch order), warmup_ms, floor_ms (the minimum of the post-warm-up runs), median_ms (the median of the same runs), runs_n, usable_runs, rounds, env_class and runner_class; its --selftest exits 1 when any of those keys is absent, when floor_ms or median_ms is not the expected value over a fixed synthetic run list, when the discarded warm-up run is included in either statistic, and when fewer than 8 post-warm-up launches produced a first_text mark. 2. fixtures/perf-budgets.json gives every ci.<runner class> a multiplier, baseline_ms, tolerance, runs_n, observed_floors_ms with at least five floors measured on main by this story, and derived_from carrying commit, runner_image and runs_n; baseline_ms equals max(observed_floors_ms) for every class; every number in the product object is byte-identical to its value before this PR, asserted by a check in the PR that reads both revisions. 3. The gate rejects a configuration that cannot do its job: node scripts/gate-perf.mjs --selftest exits 1 for each of fewer than five observed_floors_ms, baseline_ms not equal to max(observed_floors_ms), tolerance below 1.05, and (max(observed_floors_ms) / min(observed_floors_ms)) * tolerance above 1.20, each as a separately named case. 4. In ci mode the gate compares floor_ms against min(product budget * multiplier, baseline_ms * tolerance); in reference mode it compares median_ms against the product budget with no multiplier and no tolerance and never re-measures, so a 501 ms median exits 1; selftest covers a pass inside both CI rules, an envelope breach and a baseline breach. 5. The gate exits 1 when results.runs_n differs from the runs_n recorded for that runner class, proved by a selftest case, so a minimum-of-N is never compared against a baseline taken at another N. 6.
